title: Names for types
description:
A type alias gives an existing type a name that says what it is *for*.

1. Define `using Celsius = double;` and `using Fahrenheit = double;`
2. Write `Celsius toCelsius(Fahrenheit f)` using the formula (f − 32) × 5 / 9.
hints: `using Celsius = double;` makes `Celsius` another name for `double`; it is not a new type. Write both aliases at the top of the file.
Use decimal numbers in the formula (`32.0`, `5.0`, `9.0`) so nothing is done in whole numbers.
lessonTitle: auto, Type Deduction and Type Aliases
